report: Mrs. Thompson was comfortable throughout the day and participated in a family meeting to discuss her ongoing palliative care. Her daughter, Denise, joined the meeting and expressed relief knowing there is a comprehensive pain management plan. Mrs. Thompson needed full assistance with her breakfast, including cutting her food and giving her sips of water via an adapted cup. She complained of mild nausea, which was managed with prescribed medication. We turned her regularly to prevent pressure sores, and her skin remains intact.

Mr. Anderson seemed more talkative today and enjoyed listening to his favorite jazz station while browsing through a magazine. He received visitors in the afternoon, which visibly lifted his spirits. While he has no major discomfort, there was a slight increase in his restlessness, particularly in the evening. Pain relief has been administered preemptively due to his chronic back pain. Night staff noted restlessness and adjusted pillows to ensure better alignment in bed.

Ms. O'Brien participated in a small group activity today, listening to storytelling alongside other residents. She received assistance with brushing her teeth and dressing, and she noted feeling slightly better afterward. She did not have any issues with nausea today, and her skin remains healthy after the nursing team completed her regular turning schedule. A care conference took place, and her son requested regular updates on her hydration status. Ms. O'Brien tolerated her diet well, needing only encouragement for fluid intake.

Mr. Schneider required an increase in supportive care today due to observable lethargy. During the morning check-up, redness and mild oedema were noted on his heels, so we have applied protective padding and repositioning was frequently done. He had reduced appetite at lunch but managed to drink a whole cup of fortified juice. There was no incidence of choking. He engaged briefly with nurse-led reminiscence therapy and seemed mildly confused at times. His medication was reordered to ensure an uninterrupted supply.

Mrs. Patel was calm and drowsy throughout the most of the day. Her family met with the care team to discuss her symptoms and the current care plan, and they requested additional support for her nutritional needs. The hydration list indicates she met her fluid goals today. Her nails were trimmed and she was repositioned frequently to maintain skin integrity, which currently shows no issues. Pain relief was administered preventively as Mrs. Patel reported feeling a slight sensation of breathlessness. Her mobility aid was inspected to ensure stability during transfers.

Resident Aisling was quite comfortable throughout the day. She took all her meals with minimal assistance, preferring a soft, easy-to-swallow diet. Aisling was visited by her niece, and they spent a pleasant afternoon going through family photos. Despite a bit of breathlessness this morning, Aisling did not require any additional medication. Her skin is intact, and we continued with her regular turning schedule to prevent pressure ulcers.
